newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends up in nearbys as March nears expiry.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends up in nearbys as March nears expiry.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher in the nearbys, led by March, on short covering as that month neared expiration at 1201 CST Wednesday, traders said.
Firm cash basis markts, light deliveries and strong stopping plus unwinding of soybean/corn spreads led to the advances in the nearby March contract, they said.

Rolling of long positions from the March to the May boosted May with net fund buying also noted in the May as Merrill Lynch Futures bought four million bushels. Open interest (OI) in the March may have dropped 10 million bushels Monday, a trader said.
Traders early Monday said the OI was near an "uncomfortable" pre-expiry tally of 43 million bushels.
Bull spreading led to advances in the nearby months and corn held firm into the close despite a collapse in the soybean market.
Traders said the markets were technically overbought and due for volatile swings in price but corn early was boosted by a USDA monthly livestock report, the traders said.
Corn closed three cents per bushel higher to 1-1/4 lower, with March up three at $3.10-1/4 and May was up 2-1/4 at $3.06-3/4.
"It was supported a little from the cattle on feed report," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

USDA Friday said feeders placed 1.527 million cattle on feed in the seven key U.S. feeding states, or six percent more than the placements during February a year ago. Analysts were expecting a placements tally at 4.3 percent above a year ago.

Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report held no surprises, the traders said. As of Tuesday, funds were long corn by roughly 411 million bushels and short about 148.5 million bushels.

USDA's weekly export inspections report released early Monday also failed to generate any buying or selling interest. USDA said U.S. corn inspected for export during the week ended March 13 totaled 35.625 million bushels, within the range of expectations for 34 million to 38 million bushels.
Technicians early Monday cited first support in the May at $3.00 and second support at $2.92-1/4. The session low for May was $3.01-1/4.
First resistance was at $3.07-3/4 and second resistance was at $3.15-1/2. The session high for the May was $3.08.
Chartists said the four- and 20-day moving averages for the May early Monday were giving off bullish signals.
The short term nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the May closed at 64 percent. The market considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 105,000 contracts, above the 101,739 traded Friday.

In corn options, Prudential Securities sold 300 December $3.00 calls at 21 cents, sold 300 May $3.10 calls at 8-3/4 to nine cents and sold 300 May $3.10 puts at 13 cents, traders said. E.D. and F. Man International bought 300 September $2.90 puts at 21-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, about in line with the 20,529 traded Friday.
